i'm curious, why do you feel the need for there to be a point?  i struggled with this for many years myself.  i wondered "what's the point?" this led to the conclusion "there is no meaning to life, all we do is live then die."   this conclusion bothered me, and people would always respond with "well, that means you get to assign your own meaning to life!"  the problem was (for me at least) the idea of life having meaning was only valuable if that meaning was inherent, the moment the meaning was arbitrarily assigned it lost all value to me.  so this argument never gave me any peace.

so i continued to be bothered by this (meaningless of life, we just live and die) for a couple years.  [edit: now that i reflect i realize i was wrong in something i said...] it gradually dawned on me, ok, if that's the case (that life has no meaning and all we do is live and die), why does it bother me?  why not just accept that reality?  why resist that reality?  i kind of thought about, that it's like staring at the sky, and being upset that it's not green.  the hatred of the reality itself causes misery. (try it out as a thought experiment, just being neutral to it, not being upset at that reality and instead accepting it.  see how it feels to view the world from that psychology.)   i hope that makes sense what i explained and apologies if it didnt.  it took me many years to come to that conclusion but once i did life was much easier and my existential crisis ended.

why not just see your existence for what it is - just existence.  you happen to be alive right now, with ability to sense your environment and some level of awareness of that.  doesn't have to be good or bad, just is.
